messages.subject: coloring internal branches using attached data
messages.subject_clean: coloring internal branches using attached data
messages.body_plain:
I'd like to color my branches based on some data I have that can't be read in using one of ggtree's functions, so I'm using %<+% to attach the data. Unfortunately, the branches are only colored for the tips, but not the internal nodes. I got the internal node numbers following this example: ggtree(tree) + geom_text2(aes(subset=!isTip, label=node), hjust=-.3) + geom_tiplab().

Here's an example of my code:

p <- ggtree(tree, aes(color =log10(omega))) %<+% results +
    geom_tiplab(size=3) +
    geom_treescale() +
    scale_color_viridis() +
    theme(legend.position="right")

results is a data frame with the node labels (names for the tips, numbers for the internal nodes) in the first column and values I'd like to color the branches by in the second column.
> head(results)
                                     V1                           omega            p
1 Nocardia_brasiliensis_ATCC700358_esx1  0.000000     1.000000e+00
2 Nocardia_brasiliensis_ATCC700358_esxN  0.000000    1.922514e-01
3    Nocardia_cyriacigeorgica_GUH2_esxN    6.488117    2.580282e-06
4           Nocardia_farcinica_IFM_esxN         3.375098    7.255922e-06
5                                    77                        33.906093   8.611692e-09
6                                    76                        19.637654   0.000000e+00

I've attached an image of the results currently. Is there any way to get the internal branches colored as well?

messages.subject: Re: coloring internal branches using attached data
messages.subject_clean: coloring internal branches using attached data
messages.body_plain:
by default, the data (results here) will be merged by label (tip & node label) be default unless a column named 'node' exists. In that case, it will merged by 'node' number.

So, convert the 1st column to 'node' number and stored in an additional column called 'node' will solve this issue.

results$node <- NA
tipnode <- seq_along(tree$tip.label)
names(tipnode) <- tree$tip.label
results$node <- tipnode[results$V1] ## convert the tip label to tip node number
i <- is.na <http://is.na>(results$node)
results$node[i] = results$V1[i] ## fill in internal node number

p <- ggtree(tree, aes(color =log10(omega))) %<+% results +
    geom_tiplab(size=3) +
    geom_treescale() +
    scale_color_viridis() +

    theme(legend.position="right")

see also https://github.com/GuangchuangYu/ggtree/issues/47, which provides another solution by using phylo4d.

Hi, I just write a function, as.polytomy to do this. Currently it only work with phylo object and will extend to support other tree object in future.

For example, if you have a newick tree that encode bootstrap in node.label, you can use:

as.polytomy(tree, feature='node.label', fun=function(x) as.numeric(x) < 70)

messages.subject: gheatmap w layout="unrooted"?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'd like to plot an unrooted tree that illustrates the presence/absence of each tip in multiple environments.  Is it possible to do this with gheatmap, or must the tree be rectangular?  I've tried modifying the following, I run into some issues in that the unrooted plots, but the heatmap is still vertically oriented.
(identical to website, w exception that layout="unrooted" is added to ggtree: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/ggtree/inst/doc/advanceTreeAnnotation.html#visualize-tree-with-associated-matrix)

beast_file <- system.file("examples/MCC_FluA_H3.tree", package="ggtree")
beast_tree <- read.beast(beast_file)

genotype_file <- system.file("examples/Genotype.txt", package="ggtree")
genotype <- read.table(genotype_file, sep="\t", stringsAsFactor=F)
p <- ggtree(beast_tree, mrsd="2013-01-01", layout="unrooted") + geom_treescale(x=2008, y=1)
p <- p + geom_tiplab(size=3)
gheatmap(p, genotype, offset = 2, width=0.5)

The documentation associated with the function "append a heatmap of a matrix to right side of phylogenetic tree" gives me the impression what I'm hoping to do is not possible at present with this function, is that right?  Would you have any alternatives to suggest?  I've played with msaplot some as well, but also ran into similar problems.

fasta <- system.file("examples/FluA_H3_AA.fas", package="ggtree")
msaplot(ggtree(beast_tree, layout="unrooted"), fasta)

Perhaps the best alternative would be to use a geom_point or geom_tippoint and add multiple layers (one for each environment)?

Thanks for any insights,

-Matt.

For example, if the tree defaults to a width of 4 cm, but I would like to make the width 2 cm.
Is "xlim(NA,##)" the best option?

messages.subject: Re: Controlling Width of Tree Plot
messages.body_plain:
xlim is use to set the x-axis limits.

There is actually no 'absolute width' for a tree plotted in plotting device (quartz, X11, window).

You can set absolute width by saving the plot to file (pdf, png, etc) by specifying the width parameter.
